title: Decision-time progressive disclosure for learner-facing screen text
hypothesis: A neutral preregistration reflection gate will prevent producer-intent screen text before source authoring while preserving legitimate learner-facing labels.

mechanism.neutrality: Risk signals prompt both keep and remove-or-replace hypotheses; they are not presented as a verdict.
mechanism.hard_boundary: Formal registration still applies deterministic presentation-boundary and narration-duplication checks.
mechanism.zero_text_observation: Every compiled scene writes an idempotent gate_initialized observation, so an empty candidate set is distinguishable from an uninstrumented scene.

escaped_payload_descriptions: creator-persona sign-off rendered as screen text
caveats: Episode 8 predates the decision ledger, so missing attempt and prevention counts are unknown rather than zero.
The two escaped payloads were grouped in one human issue record and one scene.
The spoken persona sign-off is permitted by user policy; only its visible screen-text form belongs to this experiment.

interpretation.effectiveness_signal: Observed pre-source prevention together with fewer human screen-text escapes than Episode 8.
interpretation.quality_guardrail: Zero human screen-text boundary escapes and zero human overblocking findings; legitimate registered labels remain available to teaching scenes.
interpretation.non_claim: A same-episode rerun after the change proves tooling behavior, not cross-episode production effectiveness.
